entities.summary:
Carlo Gaetano Stampa (1667–1742) was an Italian cardinal and Archbishop of Milan from 1737 to 1742.

Born into a noble family, Stampa rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, serving as a bishop in various dioceses before being appointed Archbishop of Milan. His tenure was marked by significant reforms and appointments within the Church.

As a key figure in the Catholic Church during the early 18th century, Stampa played a crucial role in shaping the Church's policies and practices.

Stampa's legacy extended beyond his own time, as his reforms and appointments had a lasting impact on the Church's hierarchy and doctrine.

The Italian cardinal's influence can be seen in the many changes he brought to the Church during his time as Archbishop of Milan, including significant reforms in the appointment of bishops and the promotion of certain theological views.

His appointment as Archbishop of Milan was a testament to his rising influence within the Church, and his tenure marked a significant turning point in the Church's history.

The Italian cardinal's impact on the Church can still be felt today, with many of his reforms and appointments continuing to shape the Church's policies and practices.
